lines.text: Can the same nerves mean two different things?
Changing what a feeling means is called reappraisal.
Before a big grad school exam, some students were told one thing:
a racing heart can actually help you perform.
On the real math test, they scored over sixty points higher than students who weren't told.
The nerves didn't go away. Their meaning changed.
So next time your heart races, call it fuel.

post.title: Turn Nerves Into Fuel With One Thought #shorts
post.description: Same nerves, different meaning. In Jamieson, Mendes, Blackstock & Schmader (2010), students told that a racing heart can help performance scored about 64 points higher on the real GRE math section than students who weren't (a small study of 28 score reports). That's reappraisal. #psychology #anxiety #mindset
